chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding
the prayer of the two Eids, he said: 'Join the recitation with the recitation.' And he said: 'Begin with the Takbir in the first [rak'ah], then recite, then bow in the seventh [rak'ah].'

key_terms.تَصِلُ الْقِرَاءَةَ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ: Joining the recitation with the recitation (performing two recitations in one rak'ah)
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْعِيدَيْنِ: The prayer of the two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed method for performing the Eid prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ritual structure of Eid prayers, specifically emphasizing the continuity of recitation (*tasil al-qira'ah*) and the specific timing of bowing (*ruku'*) in the seventh position of the first rak'ah. It reflects the Ja'fari jurisprudential view on the precise number of extra takbirs and the method of recitation, distinguishing it from other schools by its detailed procedural guidance. The instruction to join recitations highlights the emphasis on fluidity and completeness in the liturgical performance of these festive prayers.
